title: Repository scope and the workflow contract
note: Two guards that protect other guards. repo_scope answers 'what files are in this repository' -- a question three separate red pushes got wrong by asking git grep, which sees tracked files only, so a file one commit from existing was invisible. workflow_contract answers 'does CI still run what the matrix says it runs' -- a claim that lives in YAML, which no local test would otherwise notice changing. Both are the enforcement for rows whose property is otherwise structural: R57 is enforced by an ABSENCE, and R58 by a file nothing executes locally.

mutations.name: W1_the_scope_is_tracked_files_only
mutations.rationale: the blind spot returns: a new file importing what it must not is invisible until it is committed, so the suite goes green locally and the pushed tree is red -- three times over

mutations.name: W2_the_scope_sweeps_in_ignored_files
mutations.rationale: a quarantined mutation copy or a build artifact fails guards about code that is not in the repository, which is how a structural check becomes noise people disable

mutations.name: W3_the_scope_stops_skipping_the_retired_corpus
mutations.rationale: attic/ is TRACKED -- the retired corpus, kept for history -- so removing the skip sweeps every retired module into guards about live code

mutations.name: W4_non_test_references_counts_tests_as_production
mutations.rationale: a defence whose only callers are its own tests passes the 'has a production caller' check -- the exact defect this project has hit three times

mutations.name: W5_the_symbol_search_is_not_escaped
mutations.rationale: a symbol containing regex metacharacters silently searches for something else, so a missing caller reads as present

mutations.name: W6_the_content_search_ignores_the_file_set
mutations.find:
for rel in repository_files(pattern, root=base,
                                include_tests=include_tests):
mutations.replace:
for rel in sorted(str(q.relative_to(base))
                      for q in base.rglob(pattern)):
mutations.rationale: the search and the file set disagree again, which is the disagreement this module exists to remove

mutations.name: W7_a_missing_ci_job_is_not_reported
mutations.rationale: the full-suite or second-interpreter job can be deleted and every local check still passes, while the matrix keeps claiming the coverage

mutations.name: W8_a_missing_ci_command_is_not_reported
mutations.rationale: the freshness checks, the matrix validator or the full pytest run can be removed from CI without anything noticing

mutations.name: W9_an_unwired_mutation_spec_is_not_reported
mutations.find:
if rel not in flat:
            out.append(rel)
mutations.rationale: a mutation matrix that exists on disk and runs in no CI step protects nothing on any push, and the row citing it claims hosted coverage it does not have

mutations.name: W10_an_unpinned_action_is_not_reported
mutations.rationale: a moving tag becomes acceptable, so the workflow that verifies this repository runs whatever that tag points at today

mutations.name: W11_the_uses_scan_is_anchored_to_end_of_line
mutations.rationale: every real uses: line here carries a trailing '# v4' comment, so the scan matches NOTHING and reports 'every action pinned' having examined zero actions -- the quiet failure its own test caught

mutations.name: W12_the_uses_scan_matches_prose
mutations.rationale: the workflow's own header comment about pinning is reported as an unpinned action; a guard whose first finding is its own documentation is one nobody believes
